title: 继电器 + 续流二极管：把线圈断电时的高压按住
summary: 三极管驱动 5 V 继电器，触点开关一个 9 V 电池供电的 LED。起始电路少了线圈两端的二极管：每次断电，集电极都冲到几十伏。加上它。
concepts: 电感的反向高压 inductive kick v = L·di/dt
description: GPIO → 1 kΩ → NPN 驱动 5 V 继电器线圈；继电器的 COM–NO 触点开关一个 9 V 电池供电的 LED。起始电路没有续流二极管，引脚每秒开关 10 次，集电极在每次关断时冲到约 29 V。在线圈两端反并一个二极管（色环朝 5V），尖峰就被钳在 5V 加一个二极管压降。

cards.title: 少了一个二极管
text: 面包板上已经搭好：GPIO → `1 kΩ` → 三极管 Q1，继电器 K1 的线圈接在 **5V** 脚和 Q1 的集电极之间。继电器的触点去开关一个 **9 V 电池**供电的 LED。
这个 GPIO 已经设成**每秒开关 10 次**（这种开关方式叫 PWM，5.8 再细讲），继电器“咔哒咔哒”地响。
看**诊断**：关于 K1 的线圈它说了什么？把**示波器**的探头接到 Q1 的集电极，最高冲到多少伏？

cards.title: 线圈不肯让电流马上停
text: - 线圈是一个**电感**，它像一个转起来的飞轮：电流不能一下子停。你硬要它停，它就在两端憋出很高的电压：
$$v = L \frac{di}{dt}$$
- 代入数字：线圈 150 mH，60 mA 在 0.1 ms 里被切断，$v = 0.15 × \frac{0.06}{0.0001} = 90$ V。这个电压全压在三极管上，足够把它击穿。
![](fig:kick)
- 解决办法：在线圈两端**反并一个二极管**（色环朝 5V）。平时它反偏，什么也不做。关断的一瞬间，集电极刚比 5V 高一点，它就导通，给电流一条绕回线圈的小路。
![](fig:loop)

cards.title: 把续流二极管加上
text: - **二极管** D1 并在线圈两端：**色环（阴极）接 5V 那一端**，另一端接 Q1 的集电极。插反了会把 5V 直接短路到饱和的三极管上！
- 再看诊断：线圈的警告没了。示波器上，集电极的尖峰被按住了。
- 点**「检查我的电路」**。通过后完成测量题：先预测线圈电流（线圈约 70 Ω，5V 脚比 5 V 低一点，饱和的三极管再占零点几伏）。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **线圈、电机、电磁阀：凡是电感负载，都要并续流二极管**，色环朝电源正极那一端。1N4007 或 1N4148 就够了。
- 继电器的触点和线圈**电气隔离**：控制侧 5 V，负载侧可以是完全不同的电源。
- 真实电路里的坑：买来的“继电器模块”通常已经带了三极管、二极管和指示灯，很多是低电平触发。触点写着 250 V 也不代表面包板能接市电——初学者不要碰 220 V。

caption.text: 三极管在这一刻关断：没有二极管，集电极猛地冲上去（实线）；有二极管，它刚过 5V 就被按住，线圈电流在小回路里慢慢消失（虚线）。

i18n.en: The transistor turns off at this moment: without the diode the collector shoots up (solid); with the diode it is held just above 5V while the coil current dies away in the small loop (dashed).

caption.text: 三极管一断开，线圈的电流 i 不能马上停。二极管给它一条小回路：线圈 → 二极管 → 线圈，绕几毫秒就消失了。

i18n.en: When the transistor opens, the coil current i cannot stop at once. The diode gives it a small loop — coil → diode → coil — where it dies away within a few milliseconds.

en.title: Relay + flyback diode: holding down the coil's switch-off spike
en.summary: A transistor drives a 5 V relay whose contact switches an LED on a 9 V battery. The starting board lacks the diode across the coil: at every switch-off the collector shoots to tens of volts. Add it.
en.description: GPIO → 1 kΩ → NPN drives a 5 V relay coil; the relay's COM–NO contact switches an LED on a 9 V battery. The starting board has no flyback diode, and with the pin switching 10 times a second the collector hits about 29 V at each switch-off. A reversed diode across the coil (band towards 5V) clamps the spike at 5V plus one diode drop.

cards.title: One diode missing
text: The board is already built: GPIO → `1 kΩ` → transistor Q1; relay K1's coil sits between the **5V** pin and Q1's collector. The relay's contact switches an LED powered by a **9 V battery**.
The GPIO is already set to **switch on and off 10 times a second** (this kind of switching is called PWM; more in 5.8), and the relay clicks away.
Look at the **diagnostics**: what do they say about K1's coil? Put the **scope** probe on Q1's collector: how high does it shoot?

cards.title: A coil won't let its current stop at once
text: - A coil is an **inductor**, like a spinning flywheel: its current cannot stop all at once. Force it to stop and it builds up a large voltage across itself:
$$v = L \frac{di}{dt}$$
- With numbers: a 150 mH coil whose 60 mA is cut in 0.1 ms gives $v = 0.15 × \frac{0.06}{0.0001} = 90$ V. All of it lands on the transistor, enough to break it down.
![](fig:kick)

- The fix: put a **reversed diode across the coil** (band towards 5V). Normally it is reverse-biased and does nothing. The instant the transistor turns off, the collector rises just above 5V, the diode conducts, and the current gets a small path back round the coil.
![](fig:loop)

cards.title: Add the flyback diode
text: - **Diode** D1 across the coil: **band (cathode) on the 5V end**, the other end on Q1's collector. Reversed, it would short 5V straight into the saturated transistor!
- Look at the diagnostics again: the coil warning is gone. On the scope, the collector spike is held down.

- Press **Check my circuit**. Once it passes, answer the questions; predict the coil current first (the coil is about 70 Ω, the 5V pin is a little under 5 V, and a saturated transistor takes a few tenths of a volt).

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Coils, motors, solenoid valves: every inductive load gets a flyback diode**, band towards the positive supply end. A 1N4007 or 1N4148 is enough.
- A relay's contact is **electrically isolated** from its coil: 5 V on the control side, a completely different supply on the load side.

- A real-world catch: ready-made "relay modules" usually include the transistor, the diode and an indicator LED, and many switch on when the input is LOW. A contact rated 250 V does not make a breadboard safe for mains — beginners should not touch 230 V.

compare: - Coil: (4.65 − 0.21) / 70 Ω ≈ **63 mA**, above the 53 mA pull-in current; Ib ≈ 2.53 mA, forced β ≈ 25, Q1 saturated, Vce ≈ **0.21 V**.
- Load side: (9 − 2.1) / 1 kΩ ≈ **6.8 mA**, the green LED is on.
- With D1: the collector peaks at ≈ **5.4 V** (the 5V pin + one diode drop). Without D1: about **29 V**, and a real circuit may go higher until C–E breaks down (about 40 V).

**Model note**: the coil is 70 Ω + 150 mH, pulls in at ≥ 53 mA and drops out below 7 mA, with no mechanical delay. Battery − joins GND only so the instruments share a reference; in a real project the load side can be fully separate.

measurements.ask: Output HIGH: the coil current (ammeter between the 5V pin and the coil)
measurements.explain: (4.65 − 0.21) / 70 Ω ≈ 63 mA, above the 53 mA pull-in current.

measurements.ask: Output HIGH: Vce (red lead on C, black lead on E)
measurements.explain: Ib ≈ 2.53 mA, forced β ≈ 25, still far below 150: Q1 saturates, Vce ≈ 0.21 V.

measurements.ask: Output HIGH: the LED current on the load side (9 V battery through the contact)
measurements.explain: (9 − 2.1) / 1 kΩ ≈ 6.8 mA. The contact is isolated from the coil: 5 V on the control side, any supply on the load side.

measurements.ask: Switching 10 times a second: the collector's maximum voltage Vmax on the scope
measurements.explain: As soon as D1 conducts it clamps the collector at the 5V pin voltage + one diode drop ≈ 5.4 V.

measurements.ask: Without D1 (as on the starting board), what happens the instant the transistor turns off?
measurements.explain: The coil's 63 mA has nowhere to go: the simulated collector hits about 29 V, a real one may go higher until C–E breaks down (about 40 V). With D1 the current decays around the coil → D1 loop with L/R ≈ 2 ms.
choices: the collector shoots up to tens of volts (v = L·di/dt) and may break the transistor down
the collector voltage is the same as with D1

hints: The diode goes across the coil, band (cathode) on the 5V end, plain end (anode) on the collector.
Coil between the 5V pin and C; E to GND; GPIO → 1 kΩ → B.
Load: battery + → COM, NO → 1 kΩ → LED → battery −; join battery − to the board GND.
tests: Output HIGH: relay pulls in, LED on, Q1 saturated
Output LOW: relay released, LED off, Q1 off
Switching 10 times a second: with D1 the collector spike is clamped

tests.name: 「输出 高」：继电器吸合，LED 亮，Q1 饱和
「输出 低」：继电器释放，LED 灭，Q1 截止
每秒开关 10 次：有 D1 时集电极的尖峰被钳住

compare: - 有 D1：集电极最高 ≈ **5.4 V**（5V 脚电压 + 二极管压降）。没有 D1：约 **29 V**，真实电路可能更高，直到 C–E 击穿（约 40 V）。
**模型说明**：线圈是 70 Ω + 150 mH，≥ 53 mA 吸合、< 7 mA 释放，没有机械动作时间。电池 − 接到 GND 只是为了让仪表有同一个参考点；真实项目里负载侧可以完全独立。

measurements.ask: 「输出 高」：线圈电流（电流表串在 5V 脚和线圈之间）
「输出 高」：Vce（红表笔接 C，黑表笔接 E）
measurements.explain: Ib ≈ 2.53 mA，强制 β ≈ 25，仍远小于 150：Q1 饱和，Vce ≈ 0.21 V。

measurements.ask: 「输出 高」：负载侧 LED 的电流（9 V 电池经过触点供电）
measurements.explain: (9 − 2.1) / 1 kΩ ≈ 6.8 mA。触点和线圈电气上隔离：控制侧 5 V，负载侧可以是别的电源。

measurements.ask: 每秒开关 10 次：示波器看集电极电压的最大值 Vmax
measurements.explain: D1 一导通就把集电极钳在 5V 脚电压 + 二极管压降 ≈ 5.4 V。

choices: 集电极冲到几十伏（v = L·di/dt），可能击穿三极管
集电极电压和有 D1 时一样
measurements.ask: 如果拿掉 D1（像起始电路那样），三极管关断的瞬间会怎样？
measurements.explain: 线圈的 63 mA 无处可去，仿真里集电极冲到约 29 V，真实电路可能更高，直到 C–E 击穿（约 40 V）。有 D1 时电流沿“线圈 → D1”的小回路以 L/R ≈ 2 ms 衰减。

hints: 二极管并在线圈两端：色环（阴极）接 5V 那头，另一端（阳极）接集电极。
线圈接在 5V 脚和 C 之间；E 接 GND；GPIO → 1 kΩ → B。
负载侧：电池 + → COM，NO → 1 kΩ → LED → 电池 −；电池 − 接开发板 GND。
